The codespell docs-check gate fails on 19 hits of which most are FALSE POSITIVES. 15 of them want disjointness changed to disjointedness. Disjointness is the correct term for the ontology property the SQLite schema enforces via the node_kind composite FK, and it appears in schema.sql, test_ontology.py and the archived withdrawal record. Applying the correction would corrupt the vocabulary. The right fix is an ignore-list entry in .codespellrc, not an edit. Only one hit is a real typo: sessio in bugeventlog.md line 2875.

ALL 19 codespell hits are false positives, and two classes of them would destroy records if corrected. 15 want disjointness changed to disjointedness, corrupting the ontology term the SQLite schema enforces. The other 3 flag sessio, which is not a typo but a QUOTED DEFECT: bugeventlog.md 2875 records a bad sed -i that rewrote tests/session.bats to tests/sessio.bats with the n gone, and two evidence reports quote the same corrupted string. Correcting sessio would make the defect record describe a bug that cannot happen. The only correct fix is .codespellrc ignore-words-list entries, never an edit to the prose.

row.evidence: grok audit of fde9e7b, 2026-08-01; findings medium x2 low x1
row.statement: A sidecar round-trip test can be byte-identical and still prove nothing. The session-travel lane verified sidecar -> import -> sidecar equality, which is a tautology: it re-derives the projection from the projection. The property that matters is DB -> sidecar -> DB fidelity, and it was LOSSY - measurement command, obligation blocker text and session_id are absent from the ontology projection, and retired measurements returned as synthetic placeholders with value 0. Caught by cross-vendor grok audit, missed by the architect who wrote the verification.

row.evidence: grok audit findings 1 and 2 on fde9e7b
row.statement: Basing the session sidecar on project() was the wrong foundation. project() is an ONTOLOGY projection, deliberately lossy and one-directional; the sidecar needs to be a FAITHFUL store dump because it is the conflict-resolution path for a tracked binary. Reusing project() also forced an ORDER BY into shared code, changing the existing project subcommand output. The two jobs are different and need different serialisers.

row.evidence: observed 2026-08-01: /tmp/codespell.log and /tmp/st-rework.log both 0 bytes, ps showed no matching process
row.statement: A lane detached with shell-level (cmd &) inside a wsl.exe invocation is KILLED when the wrapper exits. Two lanes dispatched that way on 2026-08-01 left 0-byte log files and no processes - they never ran, and the empty log looks identical to a lane that started and produced nothing. Long lanes must be launched through the harness background mechanism that keeps the wrapper process alive, never a bare ampersand.

row.evidence: tools/ci-local.sh gate_bats, TEST_GATE_MODE default and the RESULT PASS|SHADOW branch
row.statement: The bats gate is not switched off - it runs in SHADOW mode. tools/ci-local.sh gate_bats exports TEST_GATE_MODE defaulting to shadow, and treats both RESULT PASS and RESULT SHADOW as green, so suite failures run but cannot fail CI. row.evidence: grok audit of w1a commit a80eab0; comm -23 of scenario headings before and after
row.statement: Preserved counts do not prove preserved content. The architect verified the graph-plane spec rewrite by counting requirements (10 to 10) and scenarios (27 to 27) and called nothing weakened. A cross-vendor grok audit returned BLOCKED: 22 of 27 scenarios had been replaced, most legitimately renamed, but five dropped with no re-expression - the rename-not-deletion scenario, the pre-mutation refusal of an unguarded shared write, the reification-is-not-a-migration scenario, the health-trigger decision discipline, and the measured three-way concurrency rule whose requirement became the weaker concurrent writes cannot silently clobber. Set comparison of headings, not counts, is the check that discriminates.

row.evidence: observed 2026-08-01 checking the w1b bus-factor finding; rerunning from a staged script with the SHAs printed confirmed the auditor was right
row.statement: A before/after git comparison silently read the INDEX and produced a false no-change result. The invocation git show COMMIT:path had its command substitution stripped by the shell wrapper, leaving git show :path - which is valid syntax meaning the staged version, not an error. After a commit the index equals HEAD, so BEFORE and AFTER printed identical text and appeared to refute a correct audit finding. Any rev-resolving comparison must print the resolved SHAs alongside the output so an empty rev is visible.
